definitions: To depart from the ground and begin to fly (for an aircraft or bird).
To leave a place suddenly or quickly.
To become successful or popular very quickly.
To mimic or imitate someone or something, often humorously.
To deduct an amount from a total.
To have a period of time away from work or duties.
examples: The plane took off on time.
He took off as soon as he saw them.
The new product really took off.
He can take off his boss perfectly.
They took off 10% for cash payment.
I'm taking off next week for a holiday.
